title: Normalized slice open operations agree with the fixed ordinary open operations
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and an open immersion j:U→X of schemes. For any Operations o of [def-sf-integral-open-operations], its module extension is naturally isomorphic to the published openExtension(completed l E,j), and its module restriction is naturally isomorphic to the published proEtaleRingModulePullback along the same fixed coefficient isomorphism, as defined in [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. These are ordinary functor comparisons, before complexes or derived localization. There is no completeness, finite-field, constructibility or quasi-compactness hypothesis.

proof.text: Identify each finiteMap of o with sfCbcConstantSliceMap by the uniqueness theorem for its constant-section normalization. For the open-map/pullback site adjunction, transpose sfCompletedCoefficientMap to a map c from the open restriction of the ambient completed ring to the completed ring on U. Transposing the published completedPullMap through uniqueness of left adjoints proves c invertible. Naturality of the hom equivalence and sfCompletedCoefficientMap_existsUnique show that c respects every finite projection.

Use the concrete isomorphism from the slice forgetful functor to sliceSite followed by openMap, and its constant coefficient normalization, from the proved constant-open-restriction comparison. After forgetting commutativity, the projections of the completed ring remain jointly monic under continuous precomposition. Apply this limit extensionality and the finite-map identities to identify o.completedMap with the pushforward of c composed with that concrete site isomorphism.

The ringed pushforward adjunction along openMap and geometric base change identifies actual module pullback with pushforward using the inverse of c. Compose it with the pushforward specified by o.integralFunctor. The coefficient-map equality cancels c against its inverse; pushforward composition and the concrete site isomorphism give literal slice restriction. Whisker by o.integral.inverse and cancel its equivalence unit to obtain the desired ordinary restriction comparison. Transfer ordinaryAdjunction across this comparison and apply uniqueness of left adjoints against the published openAdjunction to obtain the extension comparison. The argument does not exclude empty or identity opens.

theorem openFactorOrdinaryTransport
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (o : IntegralOpenReduction.Operations l E j) :
    ∃ e : IntegralOpenReduction.extension l E j o ≅ openExtension (completed l E) j,
      Nonempty (IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E j o ≅
        proEtaleRingModulePullback j ((completed l E).ring X)
          ((completed l E).ring U) ((completed l E).pull j))
